sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP The Podcast, episode 192, recorded on July 11th, 2024.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 192 期，录制于 2024 年 7 月 11 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we chat with Kevlin Henney in part three of our five-part series about systems, programming, and more.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起，我们将与 Kevlin Henney 展开对话，这是我们关于系统、编程及更多内容的五集系列节目的第三部分。

sentences.en: Here's a fundamental question.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个根本性的问题。

sentences.en: Sorry, I got this.

sentences.zh: 狗狗今天早上呕吐了，所以我被委派要盯着它，这就是为什么我一直……

sentences.en: Ah, right.
sentences.zh: 啊，好的。

sentences.en: So this is, I'm sorry, I was just assuming, given that we were, you know, we're all on teams here, for those of you listening in podcast land.
sentences.zh: 所以，抱歉，我只是假设，鉴于我们，你知道，我们都在使用 Teams，对于播客听众来说。

sentences.en: And so therefore, I always thought it was compulsory when you are, you know, you're on teams, you're on Zoom or whatever, there has to be an animal.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直认为，当你使用 Teams、Zoom 或其他类似软件时，必须得有只动物在场。

sentences.en: And I just thought, I thought that Bryce was, okay, it's my turn.
sentences.zh: 我刚才还以为，我以为 Bryce 是在说，好吧，轮到我了。

sentences.en: Here is the meeting dog.
sentences.zh: 这是会议犬。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Usually I would do that for a few minutes, but in this particular case, if I see, the thing is, she's so quiet, if I didn't sit here on the bed with her, she would wander
sentences.zh: 通常我会处理几分钟，但在这种特殊情况下，如果我看到，问题是，它太安静了，如果我不坐在这里陪它，它就会走开，

sentences.en: off and potentially throw up again, and then I wouldn't know about it, and then I would get in trouble with mom, so you've got to stay here with me.
sentences.zh: 然后可能会再次呕吐，我就不知道了，然后我会被妈妈责备，所以你必须留在这里陪我。

sentences.en: I know you would like to go elsewhere, but sorry.
sentences.zh: 我知道你想去别的地方，但抱歉。

sentences.en: Anyways, the fundamental question.
sentences.zh: 总之，那个根本性的问题。

sentences.en: Fundamental question.
sentences.zh: 根本性的问题。

sentences.en: Does software get better with time?
sentences.zh: 软件会随着时间推移而变得更好吗？

sentences.en: Like, or sorry, do we get better at software over time?
sentences.zh: 或者说，抱歉，我们处理软件的能力会随着时间推移而变强吗？

sentences.en: Are things better now than they were, and will they continue to get better?
sentences.zh: 现在的情况比过去更好吗？未来会继续变好吗？

sentences.en: Ah, do you know, I think that's actually more than one question, interestingly, although you're offering different perspectives on it.
sentences.zh: 啊，你知道吗，我觉得这其实不止一个问题，很有趣，尽管你从不同的角度提出了这些问题。

sentences.en: I think collectively, we as individuals and as developers and development organizations, I think we do get better.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一个整体，无论是作为个人、开发者还是开发组织，我们确实在进步。

sentences.en: I think there are a number of things that are taken for granted now, and things that people just do that they never realized were a struggle, that they never realized was a thing
sentences.zh: 我认为现在有很多事情被视为理所当然，人们做着以前从未意识到是种挣扎、从未意识到是需要担心的事情，

sentences.en: to worry about.
sentences.zh: 现在却习以为常。

sentences.en: In fact, in digging around, I did a talk at the ACU conference in April, basically on data abstraction.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在深入研究时，我四月份在 ACU 会议上做了一个关于数据抽象的演讲。

sentences.en: I wanted to kind of focus on the history of that, but also to bring it up to date.
sentences.zh: 我当时想重点关注它的历史，但也想把它带入现代视角。

sentences.en: One of the things I looked at was Barbara Liskoff's, I've been a fan of Barbara Liskoff's
sentences.zh: 我研究的事情之一是 Barbara Liskov 的工作，多年来我一直是 Barbara Liskov 的粉丝，

sentences.en: work for many years in terms of language design, the clue language in her original work on data abstraction, but I'm nerdy like that.
sentences.zh: 在语言设计方面，比如 CLU 语言以及她最初关于数据抽象的工作，但我就是这么书呆子气。

sentences.en: So I already knew this stuff, but I saw a couple of her talks and she said, yeah, when she was given the cheering award, I think 2008,
sentences.zh: 所以我已经了解这些东西，但我看了她的一些演讲，她说，是的，当她获得图灵奖时，我想是 2008 年，

sentences.en: one of the things that one of the critics
sentences.zh: 当时网上的一位评论者说，

sentences.en: online said is, why is she getting an award for this?
sentences.zh: 为什么她会因为这个获奖？

sentences.en: Everybody knows this stuff, and they know it because she did this.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这些东西，而他们之所以知道，是因为她做了这些工作。

sentences.en: You know, prior to 1973, 1974, data abstraction was not a thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在 1973、1974 年之前，数据抽象还不是一个概念。

sentences.en: And pretty much everybody that, you know, although there was an idea of object orientation around,
sentences.zh: 几乎每个人，你知道，尽管当时有面向对象的想法，

sentences.en: her work on abstract data types had the greatest influence, particularly on statically typed languages, and the stuff that Bjarne later did, and some of the evolution of it.
sentences.zh: 但她关于抽象数据类型的工作影响最大，特别是在静态类型语言方面，以及 Bjarne 后来所做的工作，还有它的一些演变。

sentences.en: And everybody just regards it as like, yeah, yeah, of course, it's always been like this.
sentences.zh: 每个人都认为，是的，当然，它一直都是这样的。

sentences.en: It's like, no, it hasn't.
sentences.zh: 就像是，不，并不是。

sentences.en: Somebody had to do this and had to do this.
sentences.zh: 必须有人去完成这些工作。

sentences.en: And so people are able to build on a lot of features in languages, in libraries, in ecosystems, but also in the way we disseminate knowledge.
sentences.zh: 所以人们能够基于语言、库、生态系统中的许多特性进行构建，也得益于我们传播知识的方式。

sentences.en: I think, you know, we can kind of, okay, slightly egotistical from the point of view of the developer view.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，我们可以，好吧，从开发者的角度来看，这有点自负。

sentences.en: So collective egotism is a thing.
sentences.zh: 所以集体自负确实存在。

sentences.en: A lot of things have happened as a result of developers wanting to communicate.
sentences.zh: 很多事情的发生都是开发者想要交流的结果。

sentences.en: The internet, email.
sentences.zh: 互联网，电子邮件。

sentences.en: I mean, literally, it is developers trying to talk to other developers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，字面上看，这就是开发者试图与其他开发者交流。

sentences.en: How do we communicate?
sentences.zh: 我们如何交流？

sentences.en: So Usenet and therefore ultimately all forms of sharing of data.
sentences.zh: 所以有了 Usenet，最终有了所有形式的数据共享。

sentences.en: Open source, the idea, oh, guess what?
sentences.zh: 开源，这个想法，哦，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I've got a piece of code.
sentences.zh: 我有一段代码。

sentences.en: I wonder if there's a standard way we could share that and others take advantage of it.
sentences.zh: 我想知道是否有一种标准的方法可以分享它，让其他人也能受益。

sentences.en: How can we share our knowledge?
sentences.zh: 我们如何分享我们的知识？

sentences.en: Well, I'll tell you what, let's put this on a place that we can all get to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我告诉你，让我们把它放在一个我们都能访问的地方。

sentences.en: It was FTP servers and then it was World Wide Web.
sentences.zh: 先是 FTP 服务器，然后是万维网。

sentences.en: And then it was just like, it's just that we're very good at solving some of these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 然后就像是，我们非常擅长解决其中一些问题。

sentences.en: Our ability to disseminate knowledge is actually really good.
sentences.zh: 我们传播知识的能力实际上非常强。

sentences.en: So I think in the 2020s, we are definitely building on a lot of benefits that somebody from former eras would go like, wow, you know, you guys have really got it together.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在 2020 年代，我们绝对是在享受很多前人会感叹“哇，你们真的做到了”的成果。

sentences.en: But when they look closely, they might be also disappointed by, yeah, you're a bit better, but not as much better as we thought you could given all of this.
sentences.zh: 但当他们仔细观察时，他们可能会感到失望，因为“是的，你们好了一点，但并没有我们预想的那么好”。

sentences.en: So I think that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: I think that we have a benefit, but also we are not in a position where we're making the best of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有优势，但我们并没有充分利用它。

sentences.en: And then what's the statistic?
sentences.zh: 那么统计数据是什么？

sentences.en: I don't know, it varies, but half of all developers have been developing for less than a year.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，数据各不相同，但有一半的开发者开发经验不足一年。

sentences.en: It's something like that, you know?
sentences.zh: 大概就是这样，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So the influx of people is huge.
sentences.zh: 所以涌入的人数非常庞大。

sentences.en: And then trying to communicate this, if we were slightly older and stuffier, and that was the whole of the demographic, then actually we might have a different story.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要传达这一点，如果我们稍微年长一点、古板一点，而那又是全部的人口结构，那么我们可能会有不同的故事。

sentences.en: But the point is that we've got a lot of people who are coming into development and they don't have the backstory, they don't have the history, they don't see all of this
sentences.zh: 但重点是，我们有很多新人进入开发领域，他们没有背景，没有历史，他们看不到这一切，

sentences.en: or understand why such a thing is a big deal.
sentences.zh: 也不明白为什么这很重要。

sentences.en: And so therefore, they are not in a position, they're learning for the first time.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们还处于学习的初期阶段。

sentences.en: And so therefore, most developers are on the earlier part of their learning curve.
sentences.zh: 所以，大多数开发者都处于学习曲线的早期部分。

sentences.en: And I think that might characterize our profession perhaps in a different way to many other professions where there's much more of a steady state.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能以一种不同于许多其他行业的方式来定义我们的职业，在其他行业中，状态要稳定得多。

sentences.en: I think we're operating much more on a power law.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们更多是在幂律下运作。

sentences.en: So that's what may prevent us from taking full advantage of all the benefits that we actually have created.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能就是阻止我们充分利用我们实际创造的所有优势的原因。

sentences.en: But there are also all of that, all of this progress, you know, this greater interconnectedness, it comes with downsides too.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些进步，你知道，这种更强的互联性，也伴随着负面影响。

sentences.en: Like take one, like security.
sentences.zh: 比如举一个例子，安全。

sentences.en: Like in this new bold world where we have all this open source code and everything's connected,
sentences.zh: 在这个拥有所有这些开源代码且一切都相互连接的勇敢新世界里，

sentences.en: like one, like when everything's on the internet, just like the internet itself, like opened up like these attack surfaces to like almost all digital technology.
sentences.zh: 就像当一切都在互联网上时，就像互联网本身一样，几乎向所有数字技术敞开了攻击面。

sentences.en: And things like, things like, hey baby, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 还有像，像，嘿宝贝，没事的。

sentences.en: Somebody's at the door presumably.
sentences.zh: 大概是有人在敲门。

sentences.en: Things like open source and package managers have opened up supply chain attacks.
sentences.zh: 像开源和包管理器这样的东西开启了供应链攻击。

sentences.en: And that's like a whole new thing that we have to think about that we didn't have to deal with before.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全新的问题，我们必须考虑，而以前我们不必处理这些。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think, I think that's an important, that is an important thing because yeah.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我认为这是一个重要的，这是一个重要的事情，因为是的。

sentences.en: I'm going to, I'm going to have to, this may be my fridge, which they were supposed to deliver a new fridge yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我得，我得去处理一下，这可能是我的冰箱，他们昨天应该送来一台新冰箱。

sentences.en: And there's a whole story about why we have to get another new fridge because the fridge that we had was a new fridge, but I'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 关于为什么要换新冰箱还有一个完整的故事，因为我们之前的那台也是新冰箱，但我马上回来。

sentences.en: Talk amongst yourselves.
sentences.zh: 你们先聊。

sentences.en: So I'm going to pick up the point that Bryce made that, that whole, I think that, and we've seen it on the people front as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我要接着 Bryce 提出的观点说，我认为，我们在人员方面也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, it's not, it's, it's, there's a social implication here as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不是，这，这，这里也有社会影响。

sentences.en: When you start increasing connection, there's a whole lot of benefits.
sentences.zh: 当你开始增加连接时，会有很多好处。

sentences.en: There's a lot of really good network effects, but it's also an amplifier for other things and it creates new possibilities.
sentences.zh: 有很多非常好的网络效应，但它也是其他事物的放大器，并创造了新的可能性。

sentences.en: And security is one of them.
sentences.zh: 安全就是其中之一。

sentences.en: And the, the, the language or the focus on security in modern development has shifted hugely, even in just the last, even just the last five years.
sentences.zh: 而且，现代开发中对安全的语言或关注点发生了巨大的转变，即使是在过去，即使是在过去五年里。

sentences.en: And that, that is, that's not going to change, but that comes as a consequence of, yeah, connecting everything together.
sentences.zh: 而且，那，那不会改变，但这正是将一切连接在一起的结果。

sentences.en: But the assumptions that we have, it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 但我们所持有的假设，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: So yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以是的。

sentences.en: Do you remember I mentioned I worked in the electricity industry and that was in the
sentences.zh: 你还记得我提到过我在电力行业工作吗？那是在 20 世纪 90 年代，

sentences.en: 1990s and, you know, one of the things that we were working on SCADA systems, so supervisory control and data acquisition systems that sit in substations, they monitor stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们当时正在研究 SCADA 系统，即位于变电站中的监控与数据采集系统，它们监控各种东西。

sentences.en: Every electricity network has these things.
sentences.zh: 每个电力网络都有这些东西。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So you've got all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有所有这些。

sentences.en: And we were developing one of these and we, we were literally communicating between, you know, between substations and kind of headquarters using wet pieces of string.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正在开发其中一个系统，我们，我们实际上是在变电站和总部之间使用“湿绳子”进行通信。

sentences.en: We, you know, it was kind of like modem dial up speed.
sentences.zh: 我们，你知道，那就像是调制解调器拨号的速度。

sentences.en: Wait, wait, wet pieces of string.

sentences.zh: 湿绳子。

sentences.zh: 调制解调器拨号速度。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 所以对我们来说，为我们的线路级协议提供紧凑的表示非常重要，

sentences.en: because you don't have, you know, we, we worried about bandwidth in a way that people now simply wouldn't understand.
sentences.zh: 因为你没有，你知道，我们，我们对带宽的担忧是现在的人根本无法理解的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so we worried about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们担心那个。

sentences.en: That was our, one of our main things.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的，我们的主要事情之一。

sentences.en: It's like, okay, it's got to be really compact.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，它必须非常紧凑。

sentences.en: And then the question of security came up and it's just like, I remember pretty much the decision was, well, we probably don't need to worry much about security because nobody
sentences.zh: 然后安全问题出现了，我记得当时的决定基本上是，嗯，我们可能不需要太担心安全，因为没有人

sentences.en: would be stupid enough to put their, you know, their fundamental infrastructure onto the internet where it could be attacked.
sentences.zh: 会蠢到把他们的，你知道，他们的基础设施放到可能被攻击的互联网上。

sentences.en: We're already aware of worms and other issues.
sentences.zh: 我们已经意识到蠕虫和其他问题了。

sentences.en: And it's just like, yeah, but you wouldn't put the electricity grid online, would you?
sentences.zh: 就像是，是的，但你不会把电网联网，对吧？

sentences.en: No, not, not so accessible.
sentences.zh: 不，不，没那么容易访问。

sentences.en: You'd make sure that was, yeah.
sentences.zh: 你会确保那是，是的。

sentences.en: Now that's, that's charming from the modern perspective.
sentences.zh: 现在从现代的角度来看，这很迷人。

sentences.en: Um, but also it does betray the assumptions that we had because our driver was, well, the minute we start using any security, um, then that's going to involve encryption.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但这确实暴露了我们当时的假设，因为我们的驱动力是，一旦我们开始使用任何安全措施，嗯，那就会涉及加密。

sentences.en: That's going to, that's, that's potentially, or that's extra stuff.

sentences.en: If we were to use, um, uh, secure sockets that actually we lose a whole load of bandwidth by doing that.

sentences.en: So we, uh, having made everything really, really compact, uh, we'd immediately lose that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们，嗯，在把一切都做得非常非常紧凑之后，嗯，我们会立即失去它。

sentences.en: And there's a whole load of issues that we'd have with that that were performance related.
sentences.zh: 而且我们会有很多与性能相关的问题。

sentences.en: Now we, we took those decisions, um, consciously and hindsight suggests, you know what?
sentences.zh: 现在我们，我们是有意识地做出了这些决定，事后看来，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It turns out people do put this stuff on, you know, the stocks net worm was an example of
sentences.zh: 事实证明人们确实会把这些东西放到网上，你知道，震网蠕虫就是一个例子，

sentences.en: the fact, yeah, we can, we can, you can disable another country's nuclear power stations, uh,
sentences.zh: 事实是，是的，我们可以，我们可以，你可以通过互联网禁用另一个国家的核电站，嗯，哎呀，嗯，连接性的后果，那种连接性比人们预期的走得更远。

sentences.en: via the internet, um, oops, um, consequences of connectivity, that connectivity went even further than people anticipated.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所有这些问题都存在，但这确实意味着每个人现在都必须以一种他们甚至在 10 年、5 年或 10 年前只是口头上说说的方式来担心安全问题。

sentences.en: And that, you know, there are all of these issues, but it does mean everybody now has to worry about security in a way that they were only paying lip service to even only, you
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是那种就像是，是的，每个人都很关心。

sentences.en: know, 10, five or 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 你的语言必须是安全的。

sentences.en: Um, it's one of those things that's like, yeah, everybody's concerned.
sentences.zh: 你，你，你，你从上到下，你的整个堆栈，我们必须知道发生了什么，嗯，因为所有这些，事实是你的大部分软件构建都不是你自己的。

sentences.en: Your language has to be safe.
sentences.zh: 它来自其他地方，谁知道那里有什么。

sentences.en: You, you, you, you top to top to bottom, your whole stack, we have to know what's going on, um, because all of the, the fact is that most of your software build is not yours.
